history.period: Nearly 500 years old (16th century, per tradition)
history.summary: A ~500-year-old Kerala-style temple in the heart of Alappuzha town, built by King Devanarayana of Chembagasery in a jasmine garden (mulla poo thottam - 'Mullakkal' is said to derive from this). Competing origin legends: exiled soldiers from Thekkumkur brought the idol; the king dreamt of Kodungallur Bhagavathy and built the temple where his umbrella stuck in the jasmine garden; or Namboothiri refugees fleeing Tipu Sultan's conquest of Malabar installed their Annapurneswari idol here. Until 1961 the inner shrine held Annapurneswari with ladle and pot; after a stranger embraced the idol and cracks appeared, priests took it as a divine sign and installed the four-armed Rajarajeswari idol on 16 July 1962. The sanctum has an open roof; the idol faces west. Run by the Travancore Devaswom Board.

name: Mullakkal Rajarajeswari Temple
town_description: Alappuzha (Alleppey) is a coastal city in Kerala famous for its backwaters, houseboats and the annual Nehru Trophy boat race, often called the 'Venice of the East'. It is the district headquarters, well connected by rail and the NH-66 coastal highway, and a major tourism hub. The Mullakkal Rajarajeswari Temple stands in the town centre on Mullakkal Temple Road amid the busy market area.

travel.road: In Alappuzha town centre on Mullakkal Temple Road; easily reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi and local buses (verify).
